t:
Subchapter II of chapter 99 is amended by inserting in numerical sequence the following new heading:











“9902.40.87Laundry work surfaces, each comprising a molded polyvinyl chloride plastic base with backguard supply tray and having a chemical and scratch-resistant synthetic rubber work mat insert on the top surface, the foregoing designed for placement across the tops of household front-loading clothes washer and dryer pairs to make a single work surface (provided for in subheading 4016.99.05)FreeNo changeNo changeOn or before 12/31/2012”.

fable.w: This section only amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule to add a temporary duty suspension for laundry work surfaces. There is no tempting participation language at all: no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: Subchapter II of chapter 99 is amended by inserting in numerical sequence the following new heading:

qwen_block.w: This section amends a tariff schedule by adding a specific product classification and duty rate. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties in the decision-making process. The text is purely descriptive of a trade regulation amendment.
qwen_block.s: “9902.40.87Laundry work surfaces, each comprising a molded polyvinyl chloride plastic base with backguard supply tray and having a chemical and scratch-resistant synthetic rubber work mat insert on the top surface, the foregoing designed for placement across the tops of household front-loading clothes washer and dryer pairs to make a single work surface (provided for in subheading 4016.99.05)FreeNo changeNo changeOn or before 12/31/2012”.

opus.w: This section only adds a tariff heading to chapter 99 for laundry work surfaces. It sets a free duty rate and an end date of 12/31/2012. No consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government is mentioned, so the change to the tariff schedule alone does not count as participation.
opus.b:
I labelled this section **No**: it does not recommend or require participation.

1. **Tempting misreading:** There isn't a strong one. Someone might treat any change to a tariff schedule as a federal decision that outsiders could weigh in on. But the text sets up no comment period, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, consultation or right to sue.
2. **What the section actually does:** It is a tariff heading for one product. It gives the product's description, sets its duty rate to free and gives an end date for that rate. Nobody outside the federal government plays any part in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to the tariff schedule, defining a specific product code and its duty rates. It does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation, public comment, hearings, or coordination with outside parties. The text is purely definitional and regulatory in nature, lacking any procedural mechanism for external participation.
qwen_chat.s: “9902.40.87Laundry work surfaces, each comprising a molded polyvinyl chloride plastic base with backguard supply tray and having a chemical and scratch-resistant synthetic rubber work mat insert on the top surface, the foregoing designed for placement across the tops of household front-loading clothes washer and dryer pairs to make a single work surface (provided for in subheading 4016.99.05)FreeNo changeNo changeOn or before 12/31/2012”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the tariff classification implicitly involves public participation because trade regulations often go through notice-and-comment rulemaking. However, the text itself is merely a statutory amendment defining a specific tariff code and its rates; it does not explicitly mandate any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory process involving outside parties. The definition requires the section itself to recommend or require participation, not just to be subject to general administrative procedures.
